newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
INDIA THROWS OPEN CHEMICAL WEAPONS STOCKS FOR INSPECTION

India on Thursday unilaterally threw open its chemical weapons arsenal and their production and storage facilities to international inspection. But New Delhi made it clear that compliance with the Chemical Weapons Convention will not in any way compromise the security of the country should such a situation arise. As a signatory to the Convention, India submitted a list of its chemical weapons and related facilities to the Hague-based Organisation for Prohibition of the Chemical Weapons. The Indian announcement came through separate statements by the ministries of defence and external affairs.
The Economic Times
BOARD TO PROMOTE EXPORTS IN A WEEK

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Thursday announced the setting up within a week of an Export Promotion Board which will interact with exporters and solve inter-ministerial differences. It will be headed by the cabinet secretary and will include the secretaries of commerce, finance, textiles, industry, surface transport ministries and the Department of Electronics.
RELIANCE OFFERS 1:1 BONUS

Reliance Industries Ltd on Thursday announced a one-for-one bonus share issue beating market expectations of a more conservative three-for-five issue. Scores of shareholders cheered the company chairman. The Reliance scrip was marked up immediately to a high of 388 rupees on the Bombay bourse. The Reliance scrip closed lower at 377.25 rupees amid volumes of 13.18 million shares valued at 4.94 billion rupees. On the National Stock Exchange (NSE) Reliance clocked a volume of 15.81 billion rupees. The scrip rose 3.03 percent to close at 379.70 rupees on the NSE.
INDUSTRIAL FINANCE CORPORATION'S INCOME UP

The Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) logged a 32.65 percent growth in income in 1996/97 (April-March) which rose to 25.68 billion rupees from 19.36 billion rupees. The profit after tax grew to 3.79 billion rupees from 3.55 billion rupees recording a 6.67 percent rise. The corporation decided to declare a dividend of 30 percent, five percent more than the previous year. The earnings per share stand at 10.73 rupees and the book value at 41.46 rupees.
Financial Express
BANK RATE CUT WILL PROMPT MORE DOMESTIC BORROWINGS

Reserve Bank Governor Rangarajan feels that with the cut in the bank rate announced on Wednesday, there could be a shift from external commercial borrowings to domestic borrowings. He said the cut in deposit rates should lower lending rates. He ruled out any further cut in the cash reserve ratio of commercial banks soon. According to Rangarajan the lower cost of borrowings due to the deposit rate cut will prompt banks to lower their lending rates. The impact of the deposit rate cut will be substantial on banks' cost of funds, he said.
Business Standard
GAS AUTHORITY PROPOSES GDR ISSUE

The Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAlL) is set to make the country's largest-ever Global Depository Receipt offering. The government plans to divest 210 million shares of its equity holding in the company in an international share offering worth $850-900 million. This will reduce the government's stake to 71 percent. The international offering is being pegged at nearly 180 million shares worth $850 to $900 million based on the current market price of 179 rupees to 180 rupees on the major bourses. The domestic offering is proposed to be of around 30 million shares.
GENERAL ELECTRIC BULLISH ON INDIA DESPITE MODERATE GROWTH

US-based General Electric (GE) will not be able to achieve its aim of becoming a $2 billion company in India by the year 2000 butt now hopes to reach the target within the next eight years. GE is one of the largest international investors in India. The GE's projection made three years ago will not materialise mainly because of a delay in infrastructural growth. This was disclosed by the chief executive officer of GE's Indian subsidiary GE India, Scott Bayman. GE's Indian operations grew at an average rate of 20 percent to 25 percent annually in the last few years. This is much higher than the three percent growth rate in developed countries like the United States.
ICICI CUTS BORROWING RATE

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) has slashed both its long term and short term borrowing rates by 40 to 50 basis points. This follows the Reserve Bank's cut in the bank rate Wednesday by one percent. The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) is also expected to cut its rates. Following the reduction in the bank rate, demand for the five-year bonds of the IDBI rose on Thursday compared to the earlier lukewarm response. The ICICI, which was offering 14.25 percent on its five-year on-tap bonds, reduced the rates to 13.85 percent while the interest rate on its one-year paper was cut to 10.5 percent.
The Observer
ORISSA TO FLOAT BONDS FOR NRIs

The Orissa state government in collaboration with private bankers and the federal government will float investment bonds for non-resident Indians and other investors. State government officials said the state had an investment of over 10 billion rupees in various stages of clearance and implementation. Highlighting the huge investments in steel and power, these officials said the state enjoyed huge advantages in the production of steel and these would translate into tremendous cost advantage.
INDIA PROTESTS US EXPORT CURBS ON BHARAT ELECTRONICS

Minister of State of External Affairs Saleem Shervani met senior Clinton administration officials and strongly protested Washington's decision to slap curbs on US dual-technology exports to the Bharat Electronics (BEL) in Bangalore. He told the US Deputy Secretary of State and the National Security Advisor that allegations of BEL's suspected involvement and diversion of technology to India's ballistic missile programme was an "absolute canard." The Indian minister urged an expeditious lifting of the embargo.
INDIA, U.S. IN ROW OVER TELEPHONE CALL RATES

Visiting US Federal Communication Commission (FCC) Chairman Reed Hundt said India had not provided him with enough evidence to show that callback services from the United States was damaging Indian interest. But an Indian Telecom Commission member refuted the statement. A fresh controversy thus arose over Indo-US differences on international telephone traffic rates. The callback services which operate with the help of unmetred operator numbers from the United States enable users in India to make international calls as if they are made from the United States. International call rates from the United States to India are much lower than that from India to the United States.
Business Standard
RELIANCE CREATES CORPORATE HISTORY

Reliance Industries has created corporate history by becoming the first major company to announce precise targets for key financial parameters such as equity per share (EPS) growth, return on shareholder value and dividend pay-out ratio. The company said there will be no further equity increase until March 2000 and reiterated its commitment to buy back shares. The targets and future of Reliance were announced by its chairman, Dhirubhai Ambani in Bombay on Thursday. In the next five years the Reliance will strive to achieve a compounded EPS growth of 20 percent, ensure a 20 percent return on shareholder funds and regularly increase dividend rates.
